The rupee faced mounting pressure from external factors during the week, with a notable demand for dollars from oil companies and dollar sales from state-run banks. It appears that the Reserve Bank of India stepped in to mitigate further currency depreciation.

Rising crude oil prices and US bond yields kept investors on edge throughout the trading session. Broader market indices also saw a dip, reflecting the overall market sentiment. Despite some recovery, the market's fear gauge, VIX, increased significantly.

title: NSE IPO set to open for public on September 17; price band at Rs 1,700-1,785

This offer for sale will raise ₹22,561.5 crore from existing shareholders.  The issue size was reduced by fifteen percent from earlier proposals.  Share allotment is expected September 22, with listing on September 24.

title: 10-year bond yield crosses 7% as RBI trims auction bids

The Reserve Bank of India managed to accept less than half of the amount it had targeted in a three-year bond auction. Factors such as high global risk-free rates and escalating crude oil prices are exerting pressure on Indian bonds.
